scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by going through the details again to make sure I understand everything correctly. I'm a college senior, and I've been dating this guy for four months. He had been dating another girl for his first two years of college. I had a crush on him since freshman year but knew he was in a relationship. They broke up because he suspected she was cheating, based on rumors from a party. I was also at that party, but I don't remember seeing her because it was a big event with a lot of people, and our friend circles didn't overlap much. When we started dating, he was still really hurt and questioning the breakup. It was tough to see him like that, and I wanted us to have a fresh start. He asked me if I had seen his ex at the party, and I lied and said I saw her with other guys. This seemed to help him move on faster, and he's happier now without any regrets about the breakup. Now, I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for lying and keeping up the lie. I know telling the truth wouldn't gain me anything, and he's better off now. But I'm still feeling guilty about it. So, to break this down, I lied to my boyfriend about seeing his ex with other guys at a party. He used this information to confirm his suspicions that she cheated, which helped him move on and be happier. I did this because I wanted him to feel better and have a fresh start with me. On one hand, lying can be harmful because it breaks trust. If he found out, he might feel betrayed, which could damage our relationship. On the other hand, my intention was to help him heal and move forward, which seems positive. I'm also considering the consequences of telling the truth. If I had told him I didn't see her, he might have continued to be uncertain or hurt, which could have affected our relationship negatively. By lying, I gave him closure, which he needed to move on. But then, is it ever okay to lie to protect someone's feelings? I know that honesty is important, but sometimes people need to hear certain things to move on. I'm not sure where the line is between helpful deception and harmful lying. I also wonder about the long-term effects. If he never finds out, then maybe it's not that bad. But if he does find out, it could be worse. I don't know if I can live with the guilt of lying, even if it helped him in the short term. Another angle is whether I was lying to myself as well. Did I lie because I wanted to believe that his ex was at fault, or because I truly thought it would help him? I need to be honest with myself about my motivations. I also think about the concept of manipulation. By lying, am I manipulating him into feeling better about the breakup? That feels a bit underhanded, even if the outcome was positive. In the end, I'm torn between wanting to do what's best for our relationship and the moral dilemma of lying. I need to decide whether the benefits of his happiness outweigh the costs of dishonesty.
